2609.35545.title: Graph World Models for Constrained Epidemic Policy Planning
2609.35545.paper_summary: Epidemic policy planning often requires coordination between geographical regions, taking into account mobility-driven spillovers and how to make use of limited resources. Existing methods either lack action-conditioned models of coupled dynamics or cannot guarantee per-period feasibility. We present EpiMind, a graph world model framework for constrained epidemic policy planning across regions. A graph-factored recurrent state-space model generates joint policy-conditioned rollouts from regional latent beliefs, while graph-temporal ADMM optimizes regional interventions, enforces shared-resource feasibility through projection, and evaluates temporal specifications under the learned model. EpiMind reduces admission RMSE by 29% relative to graph-free dynamics modeling, plans within 1-5% of the best feasible constant policy with guaranteed shared-budget feasibility, and outperforms all deployable baselines across three resource budgets in real-context evaluation. These results demonstrate that graph-structured policy imagination with explicit constrained coordination supports effective epidemic interventions from learned dynamics.
2609.35545.paper_summary_zh: 流行病政策規劃通常需要在地理區域之間進行協調，考慮到由流動性驅動的溢出效應以及如何利用有限的資源。現有的方法要麼缺乏行動條件模型的耦合動態，要麼無法保證每個時期的可行性。我們提出了EpiMind，一個用於跨區域受限流行病政策規劃的圖形世界模型框架。一個圖形因子重複狀態空間模型從區域潛在信念生成聯合政策條件的展開，而圖形時間ADMM優化區域干預，通過投影強制共享資源的可行性，並在學習模型下評估時間規範。EpiMind相對於無圖動態建模將入院均方根誤差降低了29%，在保證共享預算可行性的情況下，計劃的結果在最佳可行恆定政策的1-5%範圍內，並在三個資源預算的實際情境評估中超越所有可部署的基準。這些結果表明，具有明確受限協調的圖結構政策想像支持從學習動態中有效的流行病干預。
